item.text:
{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q010_rossmann_family_function_divergence","answer":"SCOPe interprets these as distinct families with probable shared domain ancestry, despite divergent biological functions. In release 2.08, alcohol dehydrogenase-like C-terminal domains are family c.2.1.1 (SUNID 51736), CoA-binding domains are c.2.1.8 (51900), and potassium-channel NAD-binding domains are c.2.1.9 (63944). All belong to the NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold domains superfamily c.2.1 (51735), within fold c.2 (51734) and the alpha/beta class c (51349).

The hierarchy matters: family membership indicates a closer, clearly supported evolutionary relationship; shared superfamily membership expresses probable common ancestry across more divergent families. Shared fold alone establishes similar structural topology, not necessarily homology, and shared class describes broad secondary-structure organization. Here, SCOPe makes the stronger superfamily-level evolutionary assignment, rather than merely grouping similar folds. It does not establish orthology or identical function.

Biologically, a related structural scaffold has been adapted to different contexts: nucleotide-cofactor binding in alcohol-dehydrogenase-like proteins, CoA binding in proteins such as succinyl-CoA synthetase, and regulatory domains associated with potassium channels. This relationship concerns the specified domains, not necessarily the complete proteins. It does not imply that the CoA-binding or channel-associated domains oxidize alcohols, that the alcohol-dehydrogenase domains bind CoA or regulate channels, or that the channel-associated domain itself forms an ion-conducting pore. Nor does the superfamily or family name guarantee NAD(P) binding or oxidoreductase activity in every member.

Functional transfer requires target-specific sequence/profile evidence, conservation and geometry of ligand-contacting and catalytic residues, domain architecture, ligand-bound structural evidence, and biochemical measurements; channel-regulatory claims additionally need physiological or electrophysiological evidence. A cross-family structure can guide modeling of the conserved core, but cannot safely supply substrate specificity, catalytic chemistry, binding-loop conformations, or regulatory interactions. Prefer a close, experimentally characterized member of the target family with suitable coverage, structural quality, and ligand state; one representative cannot stand for the functional diversity of the entire superfamily.","evidence_used":["Pretrained knowledge of SCOPe hierarchy, Rossmann domains, and functional-inference limits","mcp__scope__search_scop","mcp__scope__list_scop_children","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=CoA-binding&mode=auto&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Potassium+channel&mode=auto&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51735/children?limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51735","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51735/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/63944"]}]}
